topics.name: Prepositions of place, movement and time

options: Many a bridge stand over the brook.
Many a bridge stands over the brook.
Many a bridges stands over the brook.
questions.rule: Many a takes a singular noun and a singular verb: many a bridge stands.

options: A trout jumped out of the water.
A trout jumped out from of the water.
A trout jumped out off the water.
questions.rule: Movement from inside something to outside: out of.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: flowing
flows
flown

questions.rule: Each + singular noun takes a singular verb: each little brook flows.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: since
until
on

questions.rule: Something resting on a surface takes on: leaves floating on the water.

options: live
are living
lives
questions.rule: Many a + singular noun takes a singular verb: many a fish lives.

questions.after: the stones at the bottom of the brook.
options: since
among
during
questions.rule: among = in the middle of many things. since and during are about time.

options: It joins the big river near our village.
It join the big river near our village.
It joining the big river near our village.
questions.rule: It (he/she/it) takes the simple present with -s: it joins.

options: They are under the bed.
They are under of the bed.
They is under the bed.
questions.rule: under needs no 'of', and plural they takes are.
Frequency words like never go before the main verb: never stops.

questions.source: The Ganga is the longest river in India.
options: The Ganga is longer than any other river in India.
The Ganga is long than any other river in India.
The Ganga is longest than any other river in India.
questions.rule: Superlative to comparative: longer than any other river.

options: Many a flower bloom on its banks.
Many a flower blooms on its banks.
Many a flowers bloom on its banks.
questions.rule: Many a flower blooms: singular noun, singular verb, even though the meaning is 'many'.

options: Swallows fly over the brook at summer.
Swallows fly over the brook on summer.
Swallows fly over the brook in summer.
questions.rule: Use in with seasons, months and years: in summer.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: drying
driest
dries

questions.rule: A habit with a singular subject: the brook dries up (y changes to ies).

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: wider
widest
widely

questions.rule: than needs the comparative: wider than.

options: have
are
has
questions.rule: Many a traveller is singular, so use has rested.

options: doesn't it
does it
does not it
questions.rule: never makes the sentence negative, so the tag is positive: does it?

questions.source: The river is wider than the brook.
options: The brook is not so wider as the river.
The brook is not so wide as the river.
The brook is so wide as the river.
questions.rule: Comparative to positive: The brook is not so wide as the river. Positive uses the plain adjective.

options: The brook joins the river, isn't it?
The brook joins the river, don't it?
The brook joins the river, doesn't it?
questions.rule: Simple present with joins uses does; positive sentence, negative tag: doesn't it?
among + a group of things: swim among the floating leaves.

chat: Do people still visit the old fort?
options: Yes, many a tourist visits it every year.
Yes, many a tourists visit it every year.
Yes, many a tourist visit it every year.
questions.rule: Many a tourist visits: singular noun and singular verb.

options: The brook has flowed through this valley since centuries.
The brook has flowed through this valley for centuries.
The brook has flowed through this valley from centuries.
questions.rule: Use for with a length of time (centuries, years) and since with a starting point.

options: The brook, with its many fish, sparkle in the sun.
The brook, with its many fish, sparkles in the sun.
The brook, with its many fish, sparkling in the sun.
questions.rule: The subject is the brook (singular); the phrase 'with its many fish' does not change it: sparkles.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: among
into
beside

questions.rule: beside = next to. besides means 'in addition to'.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: depending
depends
dependent

questions.rule: Many a farmer is singular: many a farmer depends.

options: clearer
most clearest
clearest
questions.rule: the ... I have ever seen needs the superlative: the clearest. Never use 'most' with -est.
Simple present question: Wh-word + does + subject + base verb: When does the brook dry up?
Many a bird drinks: 'many a' + singular noun + singular verb.

chat: The water in this brook is so clear!
options: Yes, it is clear, isn't it?
Yes, it is clear, is it?
Yes, it is clear, doesn't it?
questions.rule: Positive sentence with is takes the negative tag isn't it?

chat: Which is colder, the brook or the river?
options: The brook is colder than the river.
The brook is the colder than the river.
The brook is coldest than the river.
questions.rule: Comparing two things: colder than, with no 'the'.

options: The brook does not flow quietly.
The brook does not flows quietly.
The brook is not flow quietly.
questions.rule: Simple present negative: does not + base verb = does not flow.

options: Many a boat have sailed down this river.
Many a boat has sailed down this river.
Many a boats has sailed down this river.
questions.rule: Many a boat is singular, so the present perfect is has sailed.

options: This is the goodest spot for a picnic by the brook.
This is the most best spot for a picnic by the brook.
This is the best spot for a picnic by the brook.
questions.rule: good - better - best is irregular. Never add 'most' to best.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: swim
swimming
swum

questions.rule: Two subjects joined by both ... and are plural: Ravi and Sita swim.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: on
at
in

questions.rule: The verb depend is followed by on: depend on its water.

questions.after: rain we have had in years.
options: heavier
heaviest
heavy
questions.rule: the ... we have had in years compares with all others: superlative the heaviest.

questions.before: The brook flooded the fields last year,
options: doesn't it
wasn't it
didn't it
questions.rule: Simple past positive sentence (flooded) takes didn't it?

questions.source: No other brook in this valley is as fast as this one.
options: This is the fastest brook in this valley.
This is the faster brook in this valley.
This is the most fastest brook in this valley.
questions.rule: 'No other ... as fast as' becomes the superlative the fastest.

questions.source: The brook sings over the stones.
options: Does the brook sings over the stones?
Do the brook sing over the stones?
Does the brook sing over the stones?
questions.rule: Does + singular subject + base verb: Does the brook sing ...?
Comparative: deeper than + the thing compared.

chat: Where did you find this smooth pebble?
options: I find it among the stones near the brook.
I found it among the stones near the brook.
I found it among of the stones near the brook.
questions.rule: Past question, past answer: found. among takes no 'of'.

options: Many a stream that rise in these hills flows into the Godavari.
Many a stream that rises in these hills flows into the Godavari.
Many a streams that rise in these hills flow into the Godavari.
questions.rule: that refers to many a stream (singular), so both verbs are singular: rises ... flows.

options: The brook is more smaller than the river, but it is no less beautiful.
The brook is much smallest than the river, but it is no less beautiful.
The brook is much smaller than the river, but it is no less beautiful.
questions.rule: Use much to make a comparative stronger: much smaller than. Never 'more smaller'.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: making
makers
makes

questions.rule: The subject is Each (singular), not 'streams': each of the streams makes.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: for
at
by

questions.rule: A length of time (many years) takes for; since needs a starting point like 1990.

questions.after: lost at sea before the lighthouse was built.
options: have been
had been
were
questions.rule: Many a sailor is singular, and the loss came before the building: had been lost.
A general truth uses the simple present: the brook flows on.

chat: Is the Narmada as long as the Godavari?
options: No, it is not as longer as the Godavari.
No, it is not so long than the Godavari.
No, it is not as long as the Godavari.
questions.rule: Positive degree comparison: not as long as. 'than' goes only with comparatives.

chat: You haven't seen a real brook, have you?
options: No, I hasn't, but I would love to see one.
No, I haven't, but I would love to seen one.
No, I haven't, but I would love to see one.
questions.rule: Answer a have you? tag with I haven't (I takes have). After to, use the base verb: to see.

questions.source: Very few rivers in India are as long as the Godavari.
options: The Godavari is longer than most other rivers in India.
The Godavari is longest than most other rivers in India.
The Godavari is more longer than most other rivers in India.
questions.rule: 'Very few ... as long as' becomes longer than most other rivers.

questions.source: The brook has never dried up.
options: The brook has never dried up, hasn't it?
The brook has never dried up, has it?
The brook has never dried up, does it?
questions.rule: never makes it negative, so the tag is positive, using the helper has: has it?
